title: Monte Carlo-Based Indoor UAV Localization in Dynamic Environments Using Only Four Onboard Range Sensors
summary: Preprint (arXiv, Oct 2026), full text read. AF-MCL: 2D Monte Carlo localization in a known occupancy map from four single-point ranges plus measured yaw on a Crazyflie 2.1 with Flow and Multi-ranger decks. Likelihood field from the map EDT, beams inconsistent with the static map rejected at the previous estimate, and augmented-MCL particle injection (slow/fast likelihood averages) for kidnapping. Webots kidnapping test: recovery 2.9 s vs 16.9 s for plain MCL (simulation). Real flights in a 2.10 x 1.63 m arena: 6.4-7.7 cm mean error, filter run on a host PC, not onboard. Author list taken from the arXiv submitter and the HTML byline; not fully confirmed.
key_takeaways: Scan-to-map relocalization after kidnapping already runs on a Crazyflie with four ToF beams and a known map
Same EDT likelihood field as the hub's close-area-relocalize matcher; recovery is passive (particle injection), no hover gate and no disambiguating move
Kidnap recovery 2.9 s vs 16.9 s for plain MCL is a Webots number, not a flight number

title: Fully On-board Low-Power Localization with Multizone Time-of-Flight Sensors on Nano-UAVs
summary: DATE 2023 (venue from the AF-MCL reference list); arXiv full text read. Global Monte Carlo localization on a Crazyflie 2.1 with two 8x8-zone VL53L5CX ToF sensors and a GAP9 RISC-V processor, beam end-point (EDT) model on a 0.05 m grid. On recorded real sequences replayed with six seeds in a 31.2 m2 map: 0.15 m accuracy and above 95 % success with enough particles; the initial estimate can start in the wrong maze and converge as the drone moves. Onboard latency 0.2-30 ms depending on particle count.
key_takeaways: Map-based global localization from sparse ToF on a nano drone is published and onboard-capable
Disambiguation is passive: hypotheses resolve as the drone flies its path, not by a chosen move
Success numbers come from replayed real flight logs, not closed-loop recovery flights

title: Tackling the Kidnapped Robot Problem via Sparse Feasible Hypothesis Sampling and Reliable Batched Multi-Stage Inference
summary: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 2026 (doi 10.1109/TIM.2026.3694741, per arXiv); abstract read. Passive 2D global relocalization from one LiDAR scan against an occupancy grid while the robot stays still: RRT-sampled feasible position hypotheses, coarse ranking and early termination, and a translation-tolerant scan-to-map metric for the final pick. Ground robot with a non-panoramic LiDAR.
key_takeaways: Multi-hypothesis scan-to-map relocalization while stationary is current ground-robot practice
Picks the best hypothesis from one scan; no stated refusal to commit on near-ties

title: Nav2 AMCL configuration guide
summary: Parameter reference for the ROS 2 AMCL node (Jazzy docs, read). Likelihood-field laser model by default. Augmented-MCL random-pose injection is controlled by recovery_alpha_slow and recovery_alpha_fast, both default 0.0 (off); the docs suggest 0.001 and 0.1. Nav2 also has a ReinitializeGlobalLocalization behaviour-tree node that spreads particles over the map for a kidnapped robot.
key_takeaways: The standard ground-robot relocalizer ships with kidnap recovery switched off
Global re-initialization is a behaviour-tree action the integrator must wire in
The obvious passive baseline for any scan-to-map relocalizer on a drone

title: VOXL OpenVINS server: Initialization and Resets
summary: ModalAI docs page (read 2026-11-09). VIO starts from a static or a dynamic (about 2 s structure-from-motion) initialization. Two reset tiers: a soft reset rebuilds the filter state while keeping feature tracks; a hard reset destroys and recreates the estimator. A 30 Hz health monitor issues hard resets on estimator-health codes (bad covariance, sustained low quality, feature starvation, velocity-uncertainty breaches), never on transport warnings. The docs warn that dynamic init and soft reset can cause a jump discontinuity.
key_takeaways: Vendor VIO recovery restarts the estimator in a new frame; it does not relocalize against a prior map
Reset jumps are expected downstream, so the autopilot side must handle reset_counter

title: Conditional Variational Autoencoders for Probabilistic Pose Regression
summary: IROS 2024 (per arXiv comment); abstract read. Visual relocalization after tracking loss in scenes with repeated structure: a generative model draws camera-pose samples from the posterior given one image, so several pose hypotheses survive ambiguity. Only the submitter's name was confirmed.
key_takeaways: Multi-hypothesis relocalization under repetitive structure is an active camera-side topic
Produces hypotheses; does not choose a move to separate them

title: NanoSLAM: Enabling Fully Onboard SLAM for Tiny Robots
summary: IEEE Internet of Things Journal (doi 10.1109/JIOT.2023.3339254, per arXiv); abstract read. Lightweight end-to-end SLAM on a 44 g nano drone with a GAP9 RISC-V processor at 87.9 mW; mapping accuracy 4.5 cm and under 250 ms end-to-end, per the authors. Mapping and loop closure, not relocalization after loss. Only the submitter's name was confirmed. Code: github.com/ETH-PBL/NanoSLAM (GPL-3.0, checked with gh api).
key_takeaways: Onboard SLAM on a Crazyflie-class drone exists; it builds the map a relocalizer would need in an unknown room
Says nothing about recovery from tracking loss
